items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: in came Bunk Johnson. That's the first time I'd ever met him. And we had a session until five, six o'clock in the morning. And we turned to be great friends

ctx.x: Well, we don't want to bother you anymore, but unless there's something else you can think about, some of the other trumpet players you'd want to add about, anything about Manuel Perez or any of the others that you were especially close to?

Well, I used to like to meet up with Bunk Johnson when I... Oh, yeah. Bunk, yeah. I've recorded him. He's a particular friend of mine. I like Bunk. Well, Bunk got together in a Port Arthur one time. He said, I want to find that little fellow you all say, play so much trumpet. I want to see who he is. So, I happened to be sitting in a joint over there one night and in came Bunk Johnson. That's the first time I'd ever met him. And we had a session until five, six o'clock in the morning. And we turned to be great…
That was... Were you on that record?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: it was in the days that he was playing here with Bunk Jones, not with Bunk

ctx.x: Did you ever see him on a bicycle? Somebody was telling me he used to even ride a bicycle.

Well, if it was, it was in the days that he was playing here with Bunk Jones, not with Bunk, with what's the trumpet player, the first one? Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. Maybe in those days he might have been a younger man. He might have rode a bicycle then. You mean with that bass on his back? Yeah. Yes, I've heard him say that. I mentioned Larry Cottrell's daddy yesterday at the concert. I used to lug those drums all the way from his house up to Clay Hall Street. And then there was a whole set of drums on his…
Well, he had special drums, too, though, they said.
